title: Enterprise request caseflow sieve for hosted chat+streaming+tools
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a lightweight, audit-friendly 'caseflow sieve' to classify and prioritize incoming enterprise Hosted API feature requests that involve chat, streaming, tool/function calls, or structured outputs. The goal is to convert noisy inbound requests into deterministic lanes (quick-win, design partner, SLA/commit, blocked-by-security) with recommended routing to PM owners, SEs, and the sales intake concierge. This ticket covers the scoring rubric, intake form changes, triage runbook, and a lightweight integration into the Console intake dashboard for visibility.
acceptance_criteria: A documented scoring rubric with explicit signals (customer SLA, data sensitivity, estimated QPS, revenue at risk, compliance requirement, implementation effort) and mapping to four lanes: Quick-Win, Design-Partner, Committed SLA, Security Review
Intake form updated in Support Portal and Console with required fields for the rubric (SLA tier, expected concurrency, PII flagged, required output schema, streaming enabled, tool-call chains)
Triage Playbook that prescribes initial owner assignment rules and escalation paths, including templates for customer replies and pre-approved tech discovery checklists
A Console intake dashboard card that shows new submissions grouped by lane and a one-click 'move to canary/rollout' recommendation when appropriate
Pilot with two enterprise customers (legaltech and fintech) completed and feedback incorporated into rubric
decision_log: 2026-03-09 | PM kick-off: choose lightweight sieve vs full classifier to keep operator control. Decided to start with deterministic ruleset and telemetry signals rather than ML-based scoring.
2026-03-11 | Security review scope defined: any request with PII/data residency flagged -> mandatory security review lane

2026-03-12 | Engineering constraint: cannot guarantee per-request latency SLO changes until Dedicated/Private rollout; routing should recommend model variants and fallback policies instead of hard routing by SLA tier
